name: Asclepiades of Adramyttium
bio: Asclepiades of Adramyttium is one of the named epigrammatists whose short poems are preserved in the Greek Anthology. Paton's Index of Authors gives no date for the poet. Paton's index marks him as a contributor to the Wreath of Meleager.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fourth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XII: 36.

poems.title: Book XII, 36
poems.author: Asclepiades of Adramyttium
poems.text: Now you offer yourself, when the tender bloom is advancing under your temples and there is a prickly down on your thighs. And then you say, “I prefer this.” But who would say that the dry stubble is better than the eared corn?
